name: Docker Housekeeping
description: Real container & image health audit + safe auto-remediation. Detects unhealthy / flapping containers, dangling images, and reclaimable disk; then prunes dangling images and stopped containers when thresholds are crossed. Each remediation step is idempotent and only runs after its detection step confirms a breach. Creates a low-severity incident as the audit trail when any cleanup actually happened.

inputs.name: reclaimWarnGb
inputs.description: Fail the audit when docker can reclaim more than this many GB

inputs.name: danglingThreshold
inputs.description: Run image prune when dangling image count is strictly greater than this

inputs.name: stoppedContainerThreshold
inputs.description: Run container prune when stopped container count is strictly greater than this

steps.description: Tally containers by state (running / exited / restarting / paused / dead)
steps.command: docker ps -a --format '{{.State}}' | sort | uniq -c | awk '{ printf "%s=%d ", $2, $1 } END { print "" }'

steps.description: List unhealthy containers by name; non-zero exit when any are found so the alert pipeline picks this up
steps.command: U=$(docker ps --filter health=unhealthy --format '{{.Names}}'); if [ -n "$U" ]; then echo "UNHEALTHY: $U" | tr '\n' ',' | sed 's/,$//'; echo; exit 1; else echo 'no unhealthy containers'; fi

steps.description: Containers with high restart counts — name=restartCount for any container restarted >5 times. Pulls RestartCount from inspect for accuracy (rather than fragile status string scraping).
steps.command: F=''; for c in $(docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}}'); do RC=$(docker inspect -f '{{.RestartCount}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$RC" ] && RC=0; if [ "$RC" -gt 5 ]; then F="$F$c=$RC "; fi; done; if [ -n "$F" ]; then echo "FLAPPING: $F"; else echo 'no flapping containers'; fi

steps.description: Non-running containers — exited / dead / created. Helps spot crashed services.
steps.command: E=$(docker ps -a --filter status=exited --format '{{.Names}}({{.Status}})' | head -10); D=$(docker ps -a --filter status=dead --format '{{.Names}}' | head -5); [ -z "$E" ] && E=none; [ -z "$D" ] && D=none; echo "exited=$E dead=$D"

steps.description: docker system df — total / reclaimable bytes per resource type, machine-readable
Parse total reclaimable bytes and fail when above the warn threshold so the run is flagged
steps.command: BYTES=$(docker system df --format '{{.Reclaimable}}' | awk '{ s=$1; n=s+0; if (s ~ /GB$/) n*=1024*1024*1024; else if (s ~ /MB$/) n*=1024*1024; else if (s ~ /kB$/) n*=1024; total+=n } END { printf "%.0f", total+0 }'); GB=$(awk -v b="$BYTES" 'BEGIN { printf "%.2f", b/1024/1024/1024 }'); THRESH='${inputs.reclaimWarnGb}'; echo "reclaimable_gb=$GB threshold_gb=$THRESH"; awk -v g="$GB" -v t="$THRESH" 'BEGIN { exit !(g > t) }' && { echo 'RECLAIM_EXCEEDED'; exit 2; } || true

steps.description: Count and list a few dangling images that prune would clean up
steps.command: N=$(docker images -q --filter dangling=true | wc -l); echo "dangling_images=$N"; docker images --filter dangling=true --format '{{.ID}} {{.Repository}} {{.CreatedSince}}' | head -5

steps.description: Detect-only step: exits 0 (ok=true) when within threshold, exits 1 (ok=false) when dangling images need pruning. Drives the conditional below.
steps.command: N=$(docker images -q --filter dangling=true | wc -l); THRESH='${inputs.danglingThreshold}'; echo "dangling=$N threshold=$THRESH"; [ "$N" -le "$THRESH" ]

steps.description: Run image_prune only when check_dangling_breach failed (ok=false → dangling above threshold).
REMEDIATION: prune dangling images. Idempotent. Captures before/after dangling count and bytes freed from the prune output.
steps.command: BEFORE_N=$(docker images -q --filter dangling=true | wc -l); BEFORE_BYTES=$(docker system df --format '{{.Type}}={{.Reclaimable}}' | grep '^Images=' | head -1); OUT=$(docker image prune -f 2>&1); FREED=$(echo "$OUT" | tr -d '\n' | grep -oE 'Total reclaimed space: [^$]*' || echo 'reclaimed: unknown'); AFTER_N=$(docker images -q --filter dangling=true | wc -l); echo "REMEDIATION image_prune before_dangling=$BEFORE_N after_dangling=$AFTER_N $FREED before_reclaimable=[$BEFORE_BYTES]"

steps.description: Detect-only step: exits 0 when stopped containers within threshold, exits 1 when prune is warranted.
steps.command: N=$(docker ps -a --filter status=exited --filter status=created -q | wc -l); THRESH='${inputs.stoppedContainerThreshold}'; echo "stopped=$N threshold=$THRESH"; [ "$N" -le "$THRESH" ]

steps.description: Run container_prune only when check_stopped_breach failed.
REMEDIATION: prune stopped containers. Idempotent. Captures count removed and bytes freed.
steps.command: BEFORE_N=$(docker ps -a --filter status=exited --filter status=created -q | wc -l); OUT=$(docker container prune -f 2>&1); REMOVED=$(echo "$OUT" | grep -cE '^[a-f0-9]{12,}$' || echo 0); FREED=$(echo "$OUT" | tr -d '\n' | grep -oE 'Total reclaimed space: [^$]*' || echo 'reclaimed: 0B'); AFTER_N=$(docker ps -a --filter status=exited --filter status=created -q | wc -l); echo "REMEDIATION container_prune before_stopped=$BEFORE_N after_stopped=$AFTER_N removed=$REMOVED $FREED"

steps.description: Decide whether any remediation actually ran — used to gate the audit incident. ok=true means an incident should be created.
steps.command: IMG_OK='${steps.image_prune.ok}'; CT_OK='${steps.container_prune.ok}'; echo "image_prune.ok=$IMG_OK container_prune.ok=$CT_OK"; if [ "$IMG_OK" = "true" ] || [ "$CT_OK" = "true" ]; then echo 'audit=needed'; exit 0; else echo 'audit=skip'; exit 1; fi

steps.description: Create the audit-trail incident only when at least one remediation step succeeded.
AUDIT TRAIL: low-severity incident records that auto-remediation ran and what it touched.

params.title: Docker housekeeping auto-remediation performed
params.description: Docker housekeeping workflow auto-cleaned: image_prune.ok=${steps.image_prune.ok} container_prune.ok=${steps.container_prune.ok}. Detection: dangling=${steps.check_dangling_breach.ok} stopped=${steps.check_stopped_breach.ok} reclaim=${steps.reclaim_check.ok}. See workflow run record for full step output.

steps.description: Operator-readable rollup. Each ${steps.*.ok}=false flags an issue; remediation_*.ok=true means cleanup ran.
steps.command: echo "DockerHousekeeping: states=[${steps.container_states.ok}] unhealthy_ok=${steps.unhealthy.ok} flapping_ok=${steps.flapping.ok} reclaim_ok=${steps.reclaim_check.ok} dangling_within_threshold=${steps.check_dangling_breach.ok} stopped_within_threshold=${steps.check_stopped_breach.ok} | remediation: image_prune_ran=${steps.image_prune.ok} container_prune_ran=${steps.container_prune.ok} audit_incident_created=${steps.create_audit_incident.ok}"
